features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: The level of formal academic training the letter presents in a relevant technical field.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic architecture
features.description: Direct experience designing agent-based systems, especially with bounded autonomy, supervision, control planes, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples or improvements.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of data-structure or algorithmic strength is given.
A general claim of DS&A strength is made and anchored by at least one example.
A specific redesign or optimization story shows DS&A materially improved a real system.

features.name: Applied AI maturity
features.description: Whether the letter shows real production AI or LLM experience, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Whether the letter frames security engineering as a collaborative, developer-serving function that makes the safe path easy rather than policing or burdening others.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How consistently the letter backs its claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, named systems, counts, or other specific substantiating detail.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How strongly the letter establishes Go as a meaningful production language in the applicant's backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Whether the letter clearly states the results or effects of the applicant's work, not just the activities performed.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists duties or technologies with little sense of outcome.
Implies positive effect, but without a clear result.
States a clear before-and-after outcome for at least one contribution.
Shows vivid or quantified operational impact that explains what changed for the team.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: The breadth of programming languages the letter presents beyond the core Go and Python emphasis.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.

features.name: Narrative framing
features.description: Whether the letter has a coherent, memorable voice or thesis rather than reading like a generic checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Whether the letter shows ongoing hands-on adversarial security practice outside ordinary development work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: The extent of contribution to or responsibility for software used beyond the applicant's employer, from occasional fixes to active maintenance.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, seriousness, and self-directedness of projects the applicant describes outside normal job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: How strongly the applicant is motivated by foundational infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production ownership scope
features.description: The breadth and directness of the applicant's hands-on responsibility for production systems across testing, maintenance, launch, operation, and ownership.

levels.descriptor: Only one or two launched or maintained services are mentioned, or the scope is vague.
Roughly three or four services are mentioned, showing repeated production ownership.
Five or more services are mentioned, with explicit launch, maintenance, or testing responsibility.

features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: The amount of directly relevant full-time software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Less than 2 years of clearly relevant experience, or tenure is not stated.
About 2 to 3 years of relevant experience; clears the minimum but is still early-career for this role.
About 4 to 5 years of relevant experience; solid mid-level tenure.
6 or more years of relevant experience; deep tenure for this opening.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How convincingly the letter shows substantial, production-grade Python experience relevant to services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: Whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, failure-awareness, correctness, testing, and long-term operational care as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically the letter connects the applicant's motivations and background to this exact role and its stated responsibilities, rather than to software or security work in general.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The depth of hands-on experience the letter shows in evaluating systems for security issues and following findings through remediation or validation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: How well the letter understands the role as a security-scaling problem solved through automation, triage, tooling, and related leverage mechanisms.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The strength of formal external security certifications presented as validation of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Whether the letter conveys a thoughtful, principled commitment to security engineering itself, beyond generic interest or adjacent experience.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, prioritization, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling automation is mentioned.
Security automation is mentioned, but the triage workflow itself remains vague.
The letter clearly shows experience automating vulnerability intake, routing, or triage.
The letter describes a high-resolution triage pipeline with elements like classification, deduplication, prioritization, ownership, or clear manual-work reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree of proofreading, grammatical accuracy, and surface-level professionalism in the letter's prose.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: This captures how explicitly the letter organizes itself around the stated needs of the posting rather than leaving fit largely implicit.

levels.descriptor: Fit to the role is mostly implicit, and several core asks are left unaddressed.
Some direct alignment appears, but coverage is partial or uneven.
Most core asks are addressed clearly somewhere in the letter.
The letter deliberately maps the applicant's background to the posting's specific requirements and responsibilities.
